description: Suggested Mordheim-to-Old World crosswalk. Entries are keyed by Mordheim skill or condition ID. Partial matches and suggestions are not rules-as-written conversions; characteristic suggestions and thematic substitutions are optional house rules.

strike-to-injure.effect: +1 to injury rolls caused in hand-to-hand combat.
strike-to-injure.suggestion: +1 Strength: A simple way to represent more forceful, more damaging blows.
strike-to-injure.note: The Old World does not use Mordheim's post-wound injury roll. Killing Blow is not equivalent: it has a different trigger and effect.

combat-master.effect: An extra Attack when fighting at least two enemies, and immunity to All Alone tests.
combat-master.suggestion: +1 Attacks: Represents improved ability to handle several opponents; it loses the original outnumbered-only trigger and All Alone immunity.
combat-master.note: No general Old World rule combines a situational extra Attack with immunity to Mordheim's All Alone test.

weapons-training.effect: May use hand-to-hand weapons outside the warrior's normal equipment options.
weapons-training.suggestion: +1 Weapon Skill: A generic combat-training benefit; it does not grant access to otherwise unavailable weapons.
weapons-training.note: Old World weapon access is determined by unit equipment options; there is no general weapon-proficiency rule equivalent.

web-of-steel.effect: +1 on hand-to-hand Critical Hit table rolls.
web-of-steel.suggestion: +1 Weapon Skill: Represents more precise and controlled close-combat technique.
web-of-steel.note: Mordheim's Critical Hit table has no general Old World counterpart.

expert-swordsman.effect: May re-roll missed attacks with a qualifying sword in the turn the warrior charges.
expert-swordsman.note: Hatred allows re-rolls to hit in the first round of combat, but is not limited to swords and is not restricted to charging.

step-aside.effect: An unmodifiable 5+ extra save against close-combat wounds, after armour saves.
step-aside.suggestion: Ward Save (5+) against close-combat wounds: use as a campaign-only defensive rule; it is not a general Old World special rule.
step-aside.note: The defensive role resembles a save made after armour, but Old World ward-save values/effects are not a general skill and Mordheim's save is close-combat-only.

quick-shot.effect: May shoot twice per turn with a bow or crossbow, excluding a crossbow pistol.
quick-shot.note: Multiple Shots is a closer analogue for firing more than once; its weapon restrictions and procedures differ, so do not treat it as the same upgrade.

pistolier.effect: A brace of pistols may fire twice in the Shooting phase; a single pistol may fire in the turn it is reloaded.
pistolier.suggestion: Multiple Shots (special-rules/multiple-shots): Thematically closest for firing more than once; adapt it to pistols and do not assume its normal weapon limits match Mordheim.
pistolier.note: No general Old World rule matches the brace-of-pistols and reload benefits together.

eagle-eyes.effect: Adds 6 inches to the range of any missile weapon used.
eagle-eyes.suggestion: +1 Ballistic Skill: Improves ranged accuracy as a practical substitute, but does not extend weapon range.
eagle-eyes.note: No general Old World special rule grants this flat range increase across missile weapons.

weapons-expert.effect: May use missile weapons outside the warrior's normal warband equipment list.
weapons-expert.suggestion: +1 Ballistic Skill: A generic ranged-weapon training benefit; it does not grant access to otherwise unavailable weapons.
weapons-expert.note: Old World weapon access is determined by unit equipment options; there is no general ranged-weapon proficiency rule equivalent.

nimble.effect: May move and fire weapons that normally require the firer not to have moved; cannot combine with Quick Shot.
nimble.note: Move & Shoot is a related movement/shooting interaction, but does not reproduce Mordheim's weapon-specific restriction or its interaction with Quick Shot.

trick-shooter.effect: Ignores cover modifiers when shooting missile weapons.
trick-shooter.suggestion: +1 Ballistic Skill: Improves accuracy as a simple substitute for shooting through cover; it does not ignore cover.
trick-shooter.note: No general Old World special rule removes cover effects from shooting.

hunter.effect: May fire a handgun or Hochland long rifle every turn.
hunter.suggestion: +1 Ballistic Skill: a simple shooting benefit; this does not remove any Old World weapon reload restriction.
hunter.note: The Old World Slow Reload rule penalizes firing and therefore is not a suitable equivalent to Hunter's benefit.

knife-fighter.effect: May throw up to three throwing knives or stars, dividing shots among targets; cannot combine with Quick Shot.
knife-fighter.note: Multiple Shots is a broad analogue for extra ranged attacks, but does not match the throwing-weapon, target-splitting, or limit details.

battle-tongue.effect: Increases the leader's ability range by 6 inches.
battle-tongue.suggestion: +1 Leadership: Represents a more effective leader, but does not increase command range.
battle-tongue.note: No general Old World rule in the catalogue grants this Mordheim leader-range bonus.

sorcery.effect: +1 to rolls to determine whether a spell is cast successfully.
sorcery.suggestion: +1 Wizard Level: A suitable caster progression benefit that improves magical capability, but is broader than Mordheim's casting-success bonus.
sorcery.note: Old World casting uses different procedures; Wizard levels or casting modifiers are not a direct equivalent to this skill.

streetwise.effect: +2 to the roll for finding rare items during campaign trading.
streetwise.suggestion: +1 Initiative [campaign-adaptation]: Flavor-only campaign substitute for alertness and knowing where to look; it does not improve rare-item availability.
streetwise.note: Campaign trading and rare-item availability have no general Old World Builder rule counterpart.

haggle.effect: Once per post-battle sequence, deduct 2D6 gold crowns from one item's price, to a minimum of 1 crown.
haggle.suggestion: +1 Leadership [campaign-adaptation]: Flavor-only campaign substitute for persuasive bargaining; it does not reduce item prices.
haggle.note: This is a campaign economy benefit, not a battlefield rule represented in the Old World catalogue.

arcane-lore.effect: A qualifying warrior with a Tome of Magic may learn Lesser Magic.
arcane-lore.suggestion: +1 Wizard Level: campaign adaptation for greater magical learning; apply only to an eligible Wizard and respect the normal level cap.
arcane-lore.note: The nearest broad analogue is access to a lore of magic, but Old World lores/spells and Mordheim's Lesser Magic/Tome progression are different systems.

wyrdstone-hunter.effect: May re-roll one die on the post-battle Exploration chart when searching ruins.
wyrdstone-hunter.suggestion: +1 Initiative [campaign-adaptation]: Flavor-only campaign substitute for alert searching; it does not grant an Exploration-chart re-roll.
wyrdstone-hunter.note: Exploration and wyrdstone income are campaign mechanics without a general Old World Builder counterpart.

warrior-wizard.effect: Allows a spellcaster to wear armour and cast spells.
warrior-wizard.suggestion: Armoured Wizard: campaign-only rule allowing this model to cast spells while wearing armour; use only if the model is a Wizard.
warrior-wizard.note: Some Old World wizards can wear armour or have army-specific casting provisions, but no universal rule reproduces this skill.

mighty-blow.effect: +1 Strength in close combat, excluding pistols.
mighty-blow.suggestion: +1 Strength: The closest simple stat-based translation of the skill's increased striking power.
mighty-blow.note: A Strength characteristic increase is the closest conceptual description, but it is not a general Old World special rule and should not be substituted with a charge-only bonus.

pit-fighter.effect: While fighting inside buildings or ruins, gains +1 Weapon Skill and +1 Attack.
pit-fighter.suggestion: +1 Weapon Skill: Captures the combat-training aspect, but not the building/ruin restriction or additional Attack.
pit-fighter.note: No general Old World rule grants this terrain-dependent combination of characteristic bonuses.

resilient.effect: Reduces the Strength of close-combat hits against the warrior by 1; does not affect armour modifiers.
resilient.suggestion: +1 Toughness: The closest general stat-based way to represent resistance to injury; it is not the original Strength reduction.
resilient.note: This modifies incoming hit Strength. Armour, Regeneration, and saves in Old World work differently and are not equivalent.

fearsome.note: The named rule exists in both systems, but the tests and consequences differ.

strongman.effect: May use a double-handed weapon without its usual Always Strikes Last penalty.
strongman.note: Strike First can affect attack order against a strikes-last weapon, but it is not the same as removing that weapon's penalty and may interact differently with other rules.

unstoppable-charge.note: Furious Charge is a charge-triggered combat bonus, but its effect is not a Weapon Skill increase.

leap.effect: May leap D6 inches once per turn in addition to normal movement, including over models and obstacles.
leap.suggestion: +1 Movement: Represents greater mobility, but does not grant a separate leap or obstacle-crossing ability.
leap.note: Swiftstride affects charge/movement distance but does not grant this separate jump action or obstacle-crossing effect.

sprint.effect: May triple Movement when running or charging instead of doubling it.
sprint.note: Swiftstride affects charge distance, but does not provide Mordheim's triple movement when running or charging.

acrobat.effect: Can safely fall or jump from up to 12 inches after an Initiative test and re-roll failed Diving Charge rolls.
acrobat.suggestion: +1 Initiative: Represents agility and quick reactions, but does not reproduce safe falling or Diving Charge re-rolls.
acrobat.note: No general Old World rule combines safe falling with a diving-charge re-roll.

lightning-reflexes.effect: When charged, strikes first against the chargers; compare Initiative if they also strike first.
lightning-reflexes.note: Strike First is the closest attack-order rule, but this skill only applies when charged and has its own interaction with chargers.

jump-up.effect: Immediately stands after being knocked down and can ignore most knocked-down injury results.
jump-up.suggestion: +1 Initiative: Represents quick recovery and reactions, but does not let the model stand from a Mordheim Knocked Down state.
jump-up.note: Old World does not use Mordheim's Knocked Down injury state.

dodge.effect: May avoid a missile hit on a 5+ roll made before wounding.
dodge.suggestion: Ward Save (5+) against shooting: campaign-only defensive rule; this is a post-hit save, not Mordheim's pre-wound dodge roll.
dodge.note: A Ward Save can be a conceptually similar post-hit defence, but Dodge is a pre-wound avoidance roll against missile weapons only and is not a named general skill in Old World Builder.

scale-sheer-surfaces.effect: Can climb up or down twice normal Movement without Initiative tests.
scale-sheer-surfaces.suggestion: +1 Initiative: Represents agility while climbing, but does not provide a special climbing rule.
scale-sheer-surfaces.note: Move Through Cover does not reproduce climbing distance or the removal of Initiative tests.

knocked-down.effect: A temporary injury state that prevents fighting, shooting, and spellcasting until recovery; vulnerable to attacks in close combat.
knocked-down.suggestion: Stupidity (special-rules/stupidity): A loose thematic stand-in for impaired actions only; do not apply the normal Stupidity test or movement effects as if they were the Mordheim condition.
knocked-down.note: No direct Old World status exists in the rules index. Falling/prone models are not automatically equivalent to this injury state.

stunned.effect: The warrior does nothing until recovery; an enemy able to attack in close combat takes the warrior out of action automatically.
stunned.suggestion: Stupidity (special-rules/stupidity): A loose thematic stand-in for temporary inability to act; it does not reproduce automatic removal when attacked.
stunned.note: No direct Old World injury status exists. Failed Stupidity tests can limit actions, but are not a stun effect.

out-of-action.effect: Removed from the battle; campaign survival and serious injuries are determined after the game.
out-of-action.note: Removal as a casualty is broadly comparable to a model being slain/removed, but Old World has no matching post-battle survival and serious-injury roll.

fleeing-from-combat.effect: A warrior who fails an All Alone test breaks from combat and runs, then tests to recover on later turns.
fleeing-from-combat.note: Old World units can flee or become broken, but the unit-level break and pursuit rules differ from Mordheim's individual All Alone flight and recovery.

affected-by-fear.effect: A Fear test can restrict charging or require 6s to hit for a round of combat.
affected-by-fear.note: The named rule exists in both systems, but the test timing and effects are different.

frenzied.effect: Must charge nearby enemies, doubles Attacks in close combat, and is immune to other psychology while in charge range.
frenzied.note: Frenzy exists in both systems, but its attack bonus, charge obligations, and psychology interactions differ.

affected-by-stupidity.effect: A failed test can prevent fighting or casting and may restrict movement and shooting for the turn.
affected-by-stupidity.note: The named rule exists in both systems, but its test and consequences differ.
